arsenicism: A diseased condition produced by slow poisoning with arsenic.
aristulate: Pertaining a short beard or awn. Gray.
artistry: 1. Works of art collectively. 2. Artistic effect or quality. Southey. 3. Artistic pursuits; artistic ability. The Academy.
arnica: A genus of plants; also, the most important species (Arnica montana), native of the mountains of Europe, used in medicine as a narcotic and stimulant. Note: The tincture of arnica is applied externally as a remedy for bruises, sprains, etc.
argot: A secret language or conventional slang peculiar to thieves, tramps, and vagabonds; flash.
artiodactyla: One of the divisions of the ungulate animals. The functional toes of the hind foot are even in number, and the third digit of each foot (corresponding to the middle finger in man) is asymmetrical and paired with the fourth digit, as in the hog, the sheep, and the ox; - - opposed to Perissodactyla.
arrogate: To assume, or claim as one's own, unduly, proudly, or presumptuously; to make undue claims to, from vanity or baseless pretensions to right or merit; as, the pope arrogated dominion over kings. He arrogated to himself the right of deciding dogmatically what was orthodox doctrine. Macaulay.
archiepiscopacy: 1. That form of episcopacy in which the chief power is in the hands of archbishops. 2. The state or dignity of an archbishop.
argus: 1. (Myth.) A fabulous being of antiquity, said to have had a hundred eyes, who has placed by Juno to guard Io. His eyes were transplanted to the peacock's tail. 2. One very vigilant; a guardian always watchful. 3. (Zoöl.) A genus of East Indian pheasants. The common species (A. giganteus) is remarkable for the great length and beauty of the wing and tail feathers of the male.
articulary: A bone in the base of the lower jaw of many birds, reptiles, amphibians, and fishes.
arthrodia: A form of diarthrodial articulation in which the articular surfaces are nearly flat, so that they form only an imperfect ball and socket.
aramean: Of or pertaining to the Syrians and Chaldeans, or to their language; Aramaic. -- n. A native of Aram.
arcadia: 1. A mountainous and picturesque district of Greece, in the heart of the Peloponnesus, whose people were distinguished for contentment and rural happiness. 2. Fig.: Any region or scene of simple pleasure and untroubled quiet. Where the cow is, there is Arcadia. J. Burroughs.
arrha: Money or other valuable thing given to evidence a contract; a pledge or earnest.
archangel: 1. A chief angel; one high in the celestial hierarchy. Milton. 2. (Bot.) A term applied to several different species of plants (Angelica archangelica, Lamium album, etc.).
aromatic: Pertaining to, or containing, aroma; fragrant; spicy; strong- scented; odoriferous; as, aromatic balsam. Aromatic compound (Chem.), one of a large class of organic substances, as the oils of bitter… | A plant, drug, or medicine, characterized by a fragrant smell, and usually by a warm, pungent taste, as ginger, cinnamon spices.
archduchess: The consort of an archduke; also, a princess of the imperial family of Austria. See Archduke.
archelogy: The science of, or a treatise on, first principles. Fleming.
areolate: Divided into small spaces or areolations, as the wings of insects, the leaves of plants, or the receptacle of compound flowers.
armorist: One skilled in coat armor or heraldry. Cussans.
aristology: The science of dining. Quart. Rev.
artlessness: The quality of being artless, or void of art or guile; simplicity; sincerity.
argon: A substance regarded as an element, contained in the atmosphere and remarkable for its chemical inertness. Rayleigh and Ramsay.
arecolin: An oily liquid substance, C8H13O2N, the chief alkaloid of the betel nut, to which the latter owes its anthelmintic action.
archaeology: The science or study of antiquities, esp. prehistoric antiquities, such as the remains of buildings or monuments of an early epoch, inscriptions, implements, and other relics, written manuscripts, etc.
aruspice: A soothsayer of ancient Rome. Same as Aruspex. [Written also haruspice.]
ardent: 1. Hot or burning; causing a sensation of burning; fiery; as, ardent spirits, that is, distilled liquors; an ardent fever. 2. Having the appearance or quality of fire; fierce; glowing; shining; as, ardent eyes. Dryden. 3. Warm, applied to the passions and affections; passionate; fervent; zealous; vehement; as, ardent love, feelings, zeal, hope, temper.
arabist: One well versed in the Arabic language or literature; also, formerly, one who followed the Arabic system of surgery.
artful: 1. Performed with, or characterized by, art or skill. (old) "Artful strains." "Artful terms." Milton. 2. Artificial; imitative. Addison. 3. Using or exhibiting much art, skill, or contrivance; dexterous; skillful. He [was] too artful a writer to set down events in exact historical order. Dryden. 4. Cunning; disposed to cunning indirectness of dealing; crafty;
argive: Of or performance to Argos, the capital of Argolis in Greece. -- n. A native of Argos. Often used as a generic term, equivalent to Grecian or Greek.
arrangement: 1. The act of arranging or putting in an orderly condition; the state of being arranged or put in order; disposition in suitable form. 2. The manner or result of arranging; system of parts disposed in due order; regular and systematic classification; as, arrangement of one's dress; the Linnæan arrangement of plants. 3. Preparatory proceeding or measure; preparation;
argillocalcareous: Consisting of, or containing, clay and calcareous earth.
artless: 1. Wanting art, knowledge, or skill; ignorant; unskillful. Artless of stars and of the moving sand. Dryden. 2. Contrived without skill or art; inartistic. Artless and massy pillars. T. Warton. 3. Free from guile, art, craft, or stratagem; characterized by simplicity and sincerity; sincere; guileless; ingenuous; honest; as, an artless mind; an artless tale.
arenation: A sand bath; application of hot sand to the body. Dunglison.
arnicin: An active principle of Arnica montana. It is a bitter resin.
areopagite: A member of the Areopagus. Acts xvii. 34.
archpresbytery: The absolute dominion of presbytery. Milton.
armillary: Pertaining to, or resembling, a bracelet or ring; consisting of rings or circles. Armillary sphere, an ancient astronomical machine composed of an assemblage of rings, all circles of the same sphere, designed to represent the positions of the important circles of the celestial sphere. Nichol.
arrant: Notoriously or preëminently bad; thorough or downright, in a bad sense; shameless; unmitigated; as, an arrant rogue or coward. I discover an arrant laziness in my soul. Fuller. 2. Thorough or downright, in a good sense. (old) An arrant honest woman. Burton.
archstone: A wedge-shaped stone used in an arch; a voussoir.
argulus: A genus of copepod Crustacea, parasitic of fishes; a fish louse. See Branchiura.
arles: An earnest; earnest money; money paid to bind a bargain. [Scot.] Arles penny, earnest money given to servants. Kersey.
ariose: Characterized by melody, as distinguished from harmony. Mendelssohn wants the ariose beauty of Handel; vocal melody is not his forte; the interest of his airs harmonic. Foreign Quart. Rev.
arteriology: That part of anatomy which treats of arteries.
arminian: Of or pertaining to Arminius of his followers, or to their doctrines. See note under Arminian, n. | One who holds the tenets of Arminius, a Dutch divine (b. 1560, d. 1609). Note: The Arminian doctrines are: 1. Conditional election and reprobation, in opposition to absolute predestination. 2.
archibaldwheel: A metal-hubbed wheel of great strength and elasticity, esp. adapted for artillery carriages and motor cars.
arbitrator: 1. A person, or one of two or more persons, chosen by parties who have a controversy, to determine their differences. See Arbitration. 2. One who has the power of deciding or prescribing without control; a ruler; a governor. Though Heaven be shut, And Heaven's high Arbitrators sit secure. Milton. Masters of their own terms and arbitrators of a peace. Addison. Syn. -- Judge;
argonautic: Of or pertaining to the Argonauts.
arsenical: Of or pertaining to, or containing, arsenic; as, arsenical vapor; arsenical wall papers. Arsenical silver, an ore of silver containing arsenic.
arshine: A Russian measure of length = 2 ft. 4.246 inches.
arundelian: Pertaining to an Earl of Arundel; as, Arundel or Arundelian marbles, marbles from ancient Greece, bought by the Earl of Arundel in 1624.
architectural: Of or pertaining to the art of building; conformed to the rules of architecture. -- Ar`chi*tec"tur*al*ly, adv.
aragonite: A mineral identical in composition with calcite or carbonate of lime, but differing from it in its crystalline form and some of its physical characters.
arcual: Of or pertaining to an arc. Arcual measure of an angle (Math.), that in which the unit angle has its measuring arc equal to the radius of the circle.
armoredcruiser: A man-of-war carrying a large coal supply, and more or less protected from the enemy's shot by iron or steel armor. There is no distinct and accepted classification distinguishing armored and protected cruisers from each other, except that the first have more or heavier armor than the second.
archimedes: An extinct genus of Bryzoa characteristic of the subcarboniferous rocks. Its form is that of a screw.
arabic: Of or pertaining to Arabia or the Arabians. Arabic numerals or figures, the nine digits, 1, 2, 3, etc., and the cipher 0. -- Gum arabic. See under Gum. | The language of the Arabians. Note: The Arabic is a Semitic language, allied to the Hebrew. It is very widely diffused, being the language in which all Mohammedans must read the Koran, and is spoken…
aristocratism: 1. The principles of aristocrats. Romilly. 2. Aristocrats, collectively.
archiepiscopality: The station or dignity of an archbishop; archiepiscopacy. Fuller.
arrowroot: 1. (Bot.) A west Indian plant of the genus Maranta, esp. M. arundinacea, now cultivated in many hot countries. It said that the Indians used the roots to neutralize the venom in wounds made by poisoned arrows. 2. A nutritive starch obtained from the rootstocks of Maranta arundinacea, and used as food, esp. for children an invalids;
arachnology: The department of zoölogy which treats of spiders and other Arachnida.
arbuscle: A dwarf tree, one in size between a shrub and a tree; a treelike shrub. Bradley.
arthritic: 1. Pertaining to the joints. (old) Sir T. Browne. 2. Of or pertaining to arthritis; gouty. Cowper.
arbute: The strawberry tree, a genus of evergreen shrubs, of the Heath family. It has a berry externally resembling the strawberry; the arbute tree. Trailing arbutus (Bot.), a creeping or trailing plant of the Heath family (Epigæa repens), having white or usually rose- colored flowers with a delicate fragrance, growing in small axillary clusters, and appearing early in the spring;
arcuate: Bent or curved in the form of a bow. "Arcuate stalks." Gray.
arreptitious: Snatched away; seized or possessed, as a demoniac; raving; mad; crack-brained. (old) Odd, arreptitious, frantic extravagances. Howell.
arrenotokous: Producing males from unfertilized eggs, as certain wasps and bees.
archiater: Chief physician; -- a term applied, on the continent of Europe, to the first or body physician of princes and to the first physician of some cities. P. Cyc.
arthroderm: The external covering of an Arthropod.
arse: The buttocks, or hind part of an animal; the posteriors; the fundament; the bottom.
ardor: 1. Heat, in a literal sense; as, the ardor of the sun's rays. 2. Warmth or heat of passion or affection; eagerness; zeal; as, he pursues study with ardor; the fought with ardor; martial ardor. 3. pl. Bright and effulgent spirits; seraphim. [Thus used by Milton.] Syn. -- Fervor; warmth; eagerness. See Fervor.
ardassine: A very fine sort of Persian silk.
arrestment: 1. (Scots Law) The arrest of a person, or the seizure of his effects; esp., a process by which money or movables in the possession of a third party are attached. 2. A stoppage or check. Darwin.
areolet: A small inclosed area; esp. one of the small spaces on the wings of insects, circumscribed by the veins.
arrhizous: Destitute of a true root, as a parasitical plant.
arms: 1. Instruments or weapons of offense or defense. He lays down his arms, but not his wiles. Milton. Three horses and three goodly suits of arms. Tennyson. 2. The deeds or exploits of war; military service or science. "Arms and the man I sing." Dryden. 3. (Law) Anything which a man takes in his hand in anger, to strike or assault another with; an aggressive weapon. Cowell.
archaist: 1. Am antiquary. 2. One who uses archaisms.
arquebusade: 1. The shot of an arquebus. Ash. 2. A distilled water from a variety of aromatic plants, as rosemary, millefoil, etc.; -- originally used as a vulnerary in gunshot wounds. Parr.
arbiter: 1. A person appointed, or chosen, by parties to determine a controversy between them. Note: In modern usage, arbitrator is the technical word. 2. Any person who has the power of judging and… | To act as arbiter between. (old)
arboret: A small tree or shrub. (old) Spenser. Among thick-woven arborets, and flowers Imbordered on each bank. Milton.
arthropomata: One of the orders of Branchiopoda. See Branchiopoda.
artist: 1. One who practices some mechanic art or craft; an artisan. (old) How to build ships, and dreadful ordnance cast, Instruct the articles and reward their. Waller. 2. One who professes and practices an art in which science and taste preside over the manual execution. Note: The term is particularly applied to painters, sculptors, musicians, engravers, and architects. Elmes. 3.
arboriculture: The cultivation of trees and shrubs, chiefly for timber or for ornamental purposes.
arbitratrix: A female who arbitrates or judges.
arbitrary: 1. Depending on will or discretion; not governed by any fixed rules; as, an arbitrary decision; an arbitrary punishment. It was wholly arbitrary in them to do so. Jer. Taylor. Rank pretends to fix the value of every one, and is the most arbitrary of all things. Landor. 2.
arbitrage: 1. Judgment by an arbiter; authoritative determination. (old) 2. (Com) A traffic in bills of exchange (see Arbitration of Exchange); also, a traffic in stocks which bear differing values at the same time in different markets.
arabinose: A sugar of the composition C5H10O5, obtained from cherry gum by boiling it with dilute sulphuric acid.
archaeological: Relating to archæology, or antiquities; as, archæological researches. -- Ar`*chæ*o*log"ic*al*ly, adv.
arming: 1. The act of furnishing with, or taking, arms. The arming was now universal. Macaulay. 2. (Naut.) A piece of tallow placed in a cavity at the lower end of a sounding lead, to bring up the sand, shells, etc., of the sea bottom. Totten. 3. pl. (Naut.) Red dress cloths formerly hung fore and aft outside of a ship's upper works on holidays.
aricine: An alkaloid, first found in white cinchona bark.
arcograph: An instrument for drawing a circular arc without the use of a central point; a cyclograph.
argental: Of or pertaining to silver; resembling, containing, or combined with, silver.
argumental: Of, pertaining to, or containing, argument; argumentative.
arnee: The wild buffalo of India (Bos, or Bubalus, arni), larger than the domestic buffalo and having enormous horns.
arteriotomy: 1. (Med.) The opening of an artery, esp. for bloodletting. 2. That part of anatomy which treats of the dissection of the arteries.
artillerist: A person skilled in artillery or gunnery; a gunner; an artilleryman.
arctisca: A group of Arachnida. See Illust. in Appendix.
archtraitor: A chief or transcendent traitor. I. Watts.
arrasways: Placed in such a position as to exhibit the top and two sides, the corner being in front; -- said of a rectangular form. Encyc. Brit. Cussans.
aragonese: Of or pertaining to Aragon, in Spain, or to its inhabitants. -- n. sing. & pl. A native or natives of Aragon, in Spain.
arsenide: A compound of arsenic with a metal, or positive element or radical; -- formerly called arseniuret.
archly: In an arch manner; with attractive slyness or roguishness; slyly; waggishly. Archly the maiden smiled. Longfellow.
argol: Crude tartar; an acidulous salt from which cream of tartar is prepared. It exists in the juice of grapes, and is deposited from wines on the sides of the casks. Ure.
articularly: In an articular or an articulate manner.
arborous: Formed by trees. (old) From under shady, arborous roof. Milton.
argentous: Of, pertaining to, or containing, silver; -- said of certain silver compounds in which silver has a higher proportion than in argentic compounds; as, argentous chloride.
archbishop: A chief bishop; a church dignitary of the first class (often called a metropolitan or primate) who superintends the conduct of the suffragan bishops in his province, and also exercises episcopal authority in his own diocese.
argentamine: A solution of silver phosphate in an aqueous solution of ethylene diamine, used as an antiseptic astringent and as a disinfectant.
arrestee: The person in whose hands is the property attached by arrestment.
ariolation: A soothsaying; a foretelling. (old) Sir T. Browne.
argonaut: 1. Any one of the legendary Greek heroes who sailed with Jason, in the Argo, in quest of the Golden Fleece. 2. (Zoöl.) A cephalopod of the genus Argonauta.
aristotelian: Of or pertaining to Aristotle, the famous Greek philosopher (384-322 b. c.). -- n. A follower of Aristotle; a Peripatetic. See Peripatetic.
arab: One of a swarthy race occupying Arabia, and numerous in Syria, Northern Africa, etc. Street Arab, a homeless vagabond in the streets of a city, particularly and outcast boy or girl. Tylor. The ragged outcasts and street Arabs who are shivering in damp doorways. Lond. Sat. Rev.
arsenious: 1. Pertaining to, consisting of, or containing, arsenic; as, arsenious powder or glass. 2. (Chem.) Pertaining to, or derived from, arsenic, when having an equivalence next lower than the highest; as, arsenious acid.
arval: A funeral feast. [North of Eng.] Grose.
arbitrament: 1. Determination; decision; arbitration. The arbitrament of time. Everett. Gladly at this moment would MacIvor have put their quarrel to personal arbitrament. Sir W. Scott. 2. The award of arbitrators. Cowell.
arthrotome: A strong scalpel used in the dissection of joints.
arnaout: An inhabitant of Albania and neighboring mountainous regions, specif. one serving as a soldier in the Turkish army.
armchair: A chair with arms to support the elbows or forearms. Tennyson.
aration: Plowing; tillage. Lands are said to be in a state of aration when they are under tillage. Brande.
arrastre: A rude apparatus for pulverizing ores, esp. those containing free gold.
arborized: Having a treelike appearance. "An arborized or moss agate." Wright.
arrasene: A material of wool or silk used for working the figures in embroidery.
argue: 1. To invent and offer reasons to support or overthrow a proposition, opinion, or measure; to use arguments; to reason. I argue not Against Heaven's hand or will. Milton. 2. To prove or evince; too manifest or exhibit by inference,…
arachnologist: One who is versed in, or studies, arachnology.
arcuately: In the form of a bow.
arbutus: The strawberry tree, a genus of evergreen shrubs, of the Heath family. It has a berry externally resembling the strawberry; the arbute tree. Trailing arbutus (Bot.), a creeping or trailing plant of the Heath family (Epigæa repens), having white or usually rose- colored flowers with a delicate fragrance, growing in small axillary clusters, and appearing early in the spring;
aridity: 1. The state or quality of being arid or without moisture; dryness. 2. Fig.: Want of interest of feeling; insensibility; dryness of style or feeling; spiritual drought. Norris.
araucaria: A genus of tall conifers of the pine family. The species are confined mostly to South America and Australia. The wood cells differ from those of other in having the dots in their lateral surfaces in two or three rows, and the dots of contiguous rows alternating. The seeds are edible.
armiger: Formerly, an armor bearer, as of a knight, an esquire who bore his shield and rendered other services. In later use, one next in degree to a knight, and entitled to armorial bearings. The term is now superseded by esquire. Jacob.
arboreous: 1. Having the form, constitution, or habits, of a proper tree, in distinction from a shrub. Loudon. 2. Pertaining to, or growing on, trees; as, arboreous moss. Quincy.
armful: As much as the arm can hold.
arthrodynic: Pertaining to arthrodynia, or pain in the joints; rheumatic.
arsenite: A salt formed by the union of arsenious acid with a base.
arsenicate: To combine with arsenic; to treat or impregnate with arsenic.
archership: The art or skill of an archer.
armisonous: Rustling in arms; resounding with arms. (old)
armoric: Of or pertaining to the northwestern part of France (formerly called Armorica, now Bretagne or Brittany), or to its people. -- n. The language of the Armoricans, a Celtic dialect which has remained to the present times.
arborator: One who plants or who prunes trees. (old) Evelyn.
argentic: Pertaining to, derived from, or containing, silver; -- said of certain compounds of silver in which this metal has its lowest proportion; as, argentic chloride.
articular: Of or pertaining to the joints; as, an articular disease; an articular process. | A bone in the base of the lower jaw of many birds, reptiles, amphibians, and fishes.
armrack: A frame, generally vertical, for holding small arms.
aristotelic: Pertaining to Aristotle or to his philosophy. "Aristotelic usage." Sir W. Hamilton. ARISTOTLE'S LANTERN Ar"is*to`tle's lan"tern. (Zoöl.) The five united jaws and accessory ossicles of certain sea urchins.
archenemy: A principal enemy. Specifically, Satan, the grand adversary of mankind. Milton.
archchancellor: A chief chancellor; -- an officer in the old German empire, who presided over the secretaries of the court.
arpen: Formerly, a measure of land in France, varying in different parts of the country. The arpent of Paris was 4,088 sq. yards, or nearly five sixths of an English acre. The woodland arpent was about 1 acre, 1 rood, 1 perch, English.
are: The present indicative plural of the substantive verb to be; but etymologically a different word from be, or was. Am, art, are, and is, all come from the root as. | The unit of superficial measure, being a square of which each side is ten meters in length; 100 square meters, or about 119.6 square yards.
archipelago: 1. The Grecian Archipelago, or Ægean Sea, separating Greece from Asia Minor. It is studded with a vast number of small islands. 2. Hence: Any sea or broad sheet of water interspersed with many islands or with a group of islands.
arabin: 1. (Chem.) A carbohydrate, isomeric with cane sugar, contained in gum arabic, from which it is extracted as a white, amorphous substance. 2. Mucilage, especially that made of gum arabic.
argentan: An alloy of nicked with copper and zinc; German silver.
artsman: A man skilled in an art or in arts. (old) Bacon.
arrect: 1. Lifted up; raised; erect. 2. Attentive, as a person listening. (old) God speaks not the idle and unconcerned hearer, but to the vigilant and arrect. Smalridge. | 1. To direct. (old) My supplication to you I arrect. Skelton. 2. Etym: [See Aret.] To impute. (old) Sir T. More.
aromatization: The act of impregnating or secting with aroma.
archivist: A keeper of archives or records.
archaean: Ancient; pertaining to the earliest period in geological history. | The earliest period in geological period, extending up to the Lower Silurian. It includes an Azoic age, previous to the appearance of life, and an Eozoic age, including the earliest forms of life.
argentation: A coating or overlaying with silver. Johnson.
archaic: Of or characterized by antiquity or archaism; antiquated; obsolescent.
archipterygium: The primitive form of fin, like that of Ceratodus.
arenga: A palm tree (Saguerus saccharifer) which furnishes sago, wine, and fibers for ropes; the gomuti palm.
architecture: 1. The art or science of building; especially, the art of building houses, churches, bridges, and other structures, for the purposes of civil life; -- often called civil architecture. Many other architectures besides Gothic. Ruskin. 3. Construction, in a more general sense; frame or structure; workmanship. The architecture of grasses, plants, and trees. Tyndall.
arabian: Of or pertaining to Arabia or its inhabitants. Arabian bird, the phenix. Shak.
arcadian: Of or pertaining to Arcadia; pastoral; ideally rural; as, Arcadian simplicity or scenery.
arquebus: A sort of hand gun or firearm a contrivance answering to a trigger, by which the burning match was applied. The musket was a later invention. [Written also harquebus.]
arborary: Of or pertaining to trees; arboreal.
argolic: Pertaining to Argolis, a district in the Peloponnesus.
areolation: 1. Division into areolæ. Dana. 2. Any small space, bounded by some part different in color or structure, as the spaces bounded by the nervures of the wings of insects, or those by the veins of leaves; an areola.
archeus: The vital principle or force which (according to the Paracelsians) presides over the growth and continuation of living beings; the anima mundi or plastic power of the old philosophers. (old) Johnson.
artfully: In an artful manner; with art or cunning; skillfully; dexterously; craftily.
arrowworm: A peculiar transparent worm of the genus Sagitta, living at the surface of the sea. See Sagitta.
arterialization: The process of converting venous blood into arterial blood during its passage through the lungs, oxygen being absorbed and carbonic acid evolved; -- called also aëration and hematosis.
armless: 1. Without any arm or branch. 2. Destitute of arms or weapons.
arteriography: A systematic description of the arteries.
arcanum: 1. A secret; a mystery; -- generally used in the plural. Inquiries into the arcana of the Godhead. Warburton. 2. (Med.) A secret remedy; an elixir. Dunglison.
argonauta: A genus of Cephalopoda. The shell is called paper nautilus or paper sailor. Note: The animal has much resemblance to an Octopus. It has eight arms, two of which are expanded at the end and clasp the shell, but are never elevated in the air for sails as was formerly supposed. The creature swims beneath the surface by means of a jet of water, like other cephalopods.
arithmetical: Of or pertaining to arithmetic; according to the rules or method of arithmetic. Arithmetical complement of a logarithm. See Logarithm. -- Arithmetical mean. See Mean. -- Arithmetical progression. See Progression. -- Arithmetical proportion. See Proportion.
